title: TOPN ( 1, ..., ASC ) over -5, BLANK, 3, -1, 10 returns the BLANK row

source.quote: TOPN does not guarantee any sort order for the results
source.supports: TOPN sorts by the expression; the page does not say where BLANK goes

source.quote: If expression or value evaluates to BLANK it is treated as a 0 (zero) for all expressions that result in a number
source.supports: the other reading, documented for RANKX only: BLANK ranks as 0

derivation: Nums[N] by Id: -5 (1), BLANK (2), 3 (3), -1 (4), 10 (5). Taking BLANK as the lowest value of an ascending sort (as in assumptions/order-by-asc-blank-before-negative), the first row is Id 2.
alternative: No source states where BLANK sorts in TOPN. If TOPN ranks BLANK as 0, as RANKX is documented to, the lowest value is -5 and the result is the row Id 1, N -5.
